title: Code blue documentation
text: The recorder documents rhythm, drugs and shocks in real time on the code sheet. The team leader reviews and signs the record before the end of the shift.

title: Fever without a source in young infants
text: Infants 28 days or younger with a temperature of 38.0 C or higher get blood, urine and CSF cultures and empiric antibiotics. Older infants are risk-stratified with the step-by-step approach.

title: Blood transfusion consent and verification
text: Confirm signed consent before the first unit. Two licensed staff verify patient identity and unit details at the bedside, and vital signs are taken at 15 minutes and at the end of each unit.

title: Adult rapid response activation
text: Any staff member may call the rapid response team for acute changes in heart rate, blood pressure, breathing, oxygen saturation or mental status. The bedside nurse stays with the patient and gives a brief handoff when the team arrives.

title: Acute asthma in children
text: Give albuterol with ipratropium for three doses in the first hour and a dose of oral dexamethasone. Reassess with the pediatric asthma score after each treatment.

title: Opioid PCA monitoring
text: Monitor sedation with the Pasero scale and respiratory rate every hour for the first 24 hours of PCA. Use continuous capnography for patients with sleep apnea.
notes: Updated after PCA oversedation, pt J. Okafor MRN 01937465

title: Heparin nomogram
text: Start unfractionated heparin with an 80 units/kg bolus and an 18 units/kg/hour infusion. Check anti-Xa 6 hours after each change and adjust using the nomogram table.
notes: Nomogram check after bleed, pt D. Reyes MRN 00712290

title: Sepsis screening and early antibiotics
text: Screen adult ED and inpatient patients with qSOFA at triage and every shift. If two or more criteria are met, draw lactate and blood cultures and start broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour; repeat lactate within 2 hours if the first is above 2 mmol/L.

title: Alcohol withdrawal monitoring
text: Score withdrawal with CIWA-Ar every 4 hours, or every hour while the score is 10 or more. Give symptom-triggered lorazepam from the order set and thiamine 100 mg before any glucose.

title: Peripheral IV infiltration
text: Stop the infusion at the first sign of infiltration and remove the catheter. Elevate the limb and call pharmacy for any vesicant extravasation.

title: Massive transfusion protocol
text: Activate when the team expects to need 10 or more units in 24 hours. The blood bank releases packs of red cells, plasma and platelets in a 1:1:1 ratio until the team stops the protocol.

title: VTE prophylaxis for medical inpatients
text: Assess VTE risk with the Padua score on admission. Give enoxaparin 40 mg daily to high-risk patients unless contraindicated, and use mechanical prophylaxis while anticoagulation is held.
notes: Rev after 9/28 event, pt Maria L. MRN 00448812

title: Potassium replacement
text: Replace potassium for levels below 3.5 mmol/L. Give no more than 10 mmol per hour through a peripheral line, or 20 mmol per hour through a central line with cardiac monitoring, and recheck after every 40 mmol.

title: Insulin infusion for diabetic ketoacidosis
text: Start regular insulin at 0.1 units/kg/hour once potassium is confirmed above 3.3 mmol/L. Check glucose every hour and add dextrose 5% when glucose falls below 250 mg/dL; switch to subcutaneous insulin once the anion gap closes.

title: Stroke code door-to-needle
text: Activate a stroke code for suspected stroke within 24 hours of last known well. Aim for CT within 20 minutes of arrival, CT angiography for suspected large vessel occlusion, and thrombolysis within 60 minutes for eligible patients.

title: Hypoglycemia treatment in adults
text: For glucose below 70 mg/dL in a patient who can swallow, give 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck in 15 minutes. If the patient cannot swallow, give 25 g of dextrose 50% IV or glucagon 1 mg IM.

title: Post-operative nausea and vomiting
text: Give ondansetron 4 mg IV as first-line rescue. If nausea persists after 30 minutes, use a drug from a different class instead of repeating ondansetron.

title: Central line insertion bundle
text: Use full barrier precautions and chlorhexidine skin prep for every central line insertion. An observer completes the checklist and may stop the procedure for any break in sterile technique.

title: Neonatal jaundice screening
text: Measure transcutaneous bilirubin on all newborns at 24 to 48 hours of age or before discharge. Plot results on the hour-specific nomogram and confirm high values with a serum level.

title: Contrast allergy premedication
text: Patients with a prior moderate or severe contrast reaction get prednisone 50 mg at 13, 7 and 1 hour before the study, plus diphenhydramine 50 mg 1 hour before.

title: Chest pain evaluation pathway
text: Obtain an ECG within 10 minutes of arrival for chest pain. Use high-sensitivity troponin at 0 and 1 hour to rule out myocardial infarction.

title: Anaphylaxis management
text: Give epinephrine 0.5 mg IM into the thigh at once and repeat every 5 to 15 minutes as needed. Antihistamines and steroids are second-line and must not delay epinephrine.

title: Fall risk assessment on admission
text: Complete the Morse Fall Scale within 4 hours of admission and after any fall or transfer. Patients scoring 45 or more get a bed alarm, non-slip socks and hourly rounding.

title: Delirium screening in the ICU
text: Screen ICU patients with CAM-ICU every shift and after any change in mental status. Treat reversible causes first, limit benzodiazepines, keep a day-night routine and get patients out of bed early.

title: Hyperkalemia treatment
text: For potassium of 6.0 mmol/L or more with ECG changes, give calcium gluconate 1 g IV first. Then shift potassium into cells with insulin and dextrose and plan its removal.
notes: Case review, pt Ana P. MRN 00391827, K 6.9

title: Insulin infusion for diabetic ketoacidosis
text: Start regular insulin at 0.1 units/kg/hour once potassium is confirmed above 3.3 mmol/L. Check glucose every hour and add dextrose when glucose falls below 250 mg/dL.

title: Restraint use and monitoring
text: Restraints need a physician order renewed every 24 hours. Nursing checks circulation, skin and comfort every 2 hours and documents each release attempt.

title: Suicide risk screening
text: Screen all patients 12 and older with the C-SSRS at triage. A positive screen triggers a safety sitter and a same-day mental health evaluation.

title: Tracheostomy care
text: Clean the stoma and change the inner cannula every 8 hours. Keep a spare tracheostomy tube and obturator at the bedside at all times.

title: Pressure injury prevention
text: Assess skin with the Braden scale every shift. Reposition patients with a score of 18 or less every 2 hours and place them on a pressure-redistribution mattress.

title: Clostridioides difficile isolation
text: Place patients with suspected C. difficile on contact precautions and use soap-and-water hand hygiene. Keep precautions until 48 hours after diarrhea resolves.
